title: Sliding window
summary: Longest substring without repeats. Move the left boundary past a repeated character. O(n) time.

title: Two pointers
summary: Find two values summing to a target in a sorted list. Return their indices or None. O(n) time.

title: Fast and slow pointers
summary: Detect a cycle in a linked list using constant extra space. The fast pointer takes two steps.

title: Merge intervals
summary: Merge overlapping closed intervals. Assume each start is at most its end. O(n log n) time.

title: Binary search
summary: Find the first index whose value is at least target in a sorted list. The search interval is [left, right).

title: Prefix sums and a hash map
summary: Count subarrays summing to a target, including when values are negative. Seed the empty prefix once.

title: Monotonic stack
summary: For each temperature, count days until a warmer day. Store unresolved indices in decreasing temperature order.

title: Breadth-first search
summary: Shortest edge distances in an unweighted adjacency map. Mark a node when enqueuing it, not when removing it.

title: Depth-first search
summary: Visit reachable nodes in an adjacency map. An explicit stack avoids recursion-depth limits.

title: Backtracking
summary: Generate all subsets of a list of distinct values. Choose, explore, undo; copy the current path before saving it.
code:
# Each recursive call extends a choice made so far.
def subsets(values):
    result = []
    path = []
    def visit(start):
        result.append(path.copy())
        for index in range(start, len(values)):
            path.append(values[index])
            visit(index + 1)
            path.pop()
    visit(0)
    return result

title: Top K with a heap
summary: Keep only the k largest values using a min-heap. Returns up to k values in descending order. O(n log k) for 1 ≤ k ≤ n.

title: Union-find
summary: Track connected components among nodes 0 through n-1. Use path compression and union by size.

title: Dynamic programming
summary: Maximum sum of nonadjacent nonnegative values. Keep only the previous two optimal states. O(n) time, O(1) extra space.
code:
# Choose between skipping this value and taking it.
def max_nonadjacent_sum(values):
    previous_two = 0
    previous_one = 0
    for value in values:
        current = max(previous_one, previous_two + value)
        previous_two = previous_one
        previous_one = current
    return previous_one

summary: A pointer receiver mutates the original struct. A value receiver can inspect a copy.

summary: Types satisfy interfaces implicitly. Accept the behavior you need as a small interface.

title: Thread pool and futures
summary: Submit independent tasks and retrieve results in input order. Threads commonly suit blocking I/O; this arithmetic task only demonstrates the API.
code:
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

def square(value):
    return value * value

def parallel_squares(values):
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as executor:
        futures = [executor.submit(square, value) for value in values]
        return [future.result() for future in futures]

title: Protecting shared state
summary: A lock protects the complete read-modify-write operation. Join every worker before observing the final result.

title: Async tasks with gather
summary: Await cooperative work without blocking the event loop. gather returns results in argument order. Run the demo from a normal Python script.
code:
import asyncio

async def work(value):
    await asyncio.sleep(0)
    return value * 2

async def run_batch(values):
    tasks = [work(value) for value in values]
    return await asyncio.gather(*tasks)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(asyncio.run(run_batch([1, 2, 3])))

title: Mutex and lock_guard
summary: C++17. Hold a scoped mutex guard around shared state. Join both threads before reading the counter.

title: Condition variable and a predicate
summary: C++17. The predicate handles notifications that arrive early and spurious wakeups. Both data and readiness are protected by the same mutex.

title: Async and future
summary: C++17. Request asynchronous execution explicitly, retain the future and collect its value with get.

title: Goroutines, channels and closing
summary: The sender closes the channel after producing all values. range receives until the channel is closed and drained.

title: Arc, Mutex and thread joining
summary: Arc shares ownership across threads; Mutex serializes mutation. This small demo treats a panicked worker or poisoned mutex as fatal.
